paragraphs.text: וַיְצַ֞ו אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־בֵּיתוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ מַלֵּ֞א אֶת־אַמְתְּחֹ֤ת הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֹ֔כֶל כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יוּכְל֖וּן שְׂאֵ֑ת וְשִׂ֥ים כֶּֽסֶף־אִ֖ישׁ בְּפִ֥י אַמְתַּחְתּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he commanded him that was over his house, saying, Fill the men's sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man's money in his sack's mouth.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־גְּבִיעִ֞י גְּבִ֣יעַ הַכֶּ֗סֶף תָּשִׂים֙ בְּפִי֙ אַמְתַּ֣חַת הַקָּטֹ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת כֶּ֣סֶף שִׁבְר֑וֹ וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כִּדְבַ֥ר יוֹסֵ֖ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃

i18n.en: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack's mouth of the youngest, and his grain money. And he did according to the word that Yosef had spoken.

paragraphs.commentary: The silver cup (*gevia ha-kesef*) planted in Binyamin's sack is the chapter's central object — and, as v 5 will name, the divinatory-instrument that Yosef the *shallit* claims to use. The *kesef shivro* construction pairs the silver-money with the *shever* (the grain-as-commodity) governed by the central `shever-mashbir-grain-purchase-vocabulary-yosef-cycle` entry, whose scope is now extended to include the Gen 44:2 and 44:25 occurrences in the chapter.

paragraphs.text: הַבֹּ֖קֶר א֑וֹר וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים שֻׁלְּח֔וּ הֵ֖מָּה וַחֲמֹרֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their asses.

paragraphs.text: הֵ֠ם יָֽצְא֣וּ אֶת־הָעִיר֮ לֹ֣א הִרְחִיקוּ֒ וְיוֹסֵ֤ף אָמַר֙ לַֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־בֵּית֔וֹ ק֥וּם רְדֹ֖ף אַחֲרֵ֣י הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְהִשַּׂגְתָּם֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם לָ֛מָּה שִׁלַּמְתֶּ֥ם רָעָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת טוֹבָֽה׃

i18n.en: And when they were gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Yosef said unto his steward, Up, follow after the men; and when thou dost overtake them, say unto them, Wherefore have ye rewarded evil for good?

paragraphs.commentary: *Lammah shillamtem ra'ah tachat tovah* — 'wherefore have ye rewarded evil for good?' — deploys the standard HB moral-reversal formula (Piel of *shalem* + *tachat* + abstract-noun pair). The construction recurs across the wisdom-and-Psalmic indictment-of-injustice tradition (Prov 17:13; Ps 35:12; 38:21; 109:5; Jer 18:20; 1 Sam 25:21). The accusation is doubly-ironic: the brothers have not stolen the cup (so the immediate-accusation is false), but they have repaid evil-for-good in the Gen 37 transaction (so the deeper-accusation is true). The literary point — that the false-allegation echoes the actual-guilt — is the chapter's signature ethical-architecture. Governed by the new overlay `shillamtem-raah-tachat-tovah-evil-for-good-formula-gen44`.

paragraphs.text: הֲל֣וֹא זֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁתֶּ֤ה אֲדֹנִי֙ בּ֔וֹ וְה֕וּא נַחֵ֥שׁ יְנַחֵ֖שׁ בּ֑וֹ הֲרֵעֹתֶ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲשִׂיתֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Is not this it in which my lord drinketh, and whereby he indeed divineth? ye have done evil in so doing.

paragraphs.commentary: The Piel of *nachash* II (*nachesh yenachesh*, the paronomastic infinitive-absolute intensifier 'indeed divineth') names the cup as the divinatory-instrument. The lexeme is the corpus's standard divination-verb, governed across the Deuteronomic prohibition-list (Deut 18:10 *menachesh* among the *to'evot* the *goyim* practice), the H-Code (Lev 19:26 *lo tenachashu*), the Bil'am cycle (Num 23:23, 24:1), the Deuteronomistic indictments (2 Kgs 17:17, 21:6 = 2 Chr 33:6), and Isa 2:6. The Gen 44:5 + 15 deployment is the only HB scene in which Yosef is portrayed as using divination — and only as a ruse, the maintained-disguise of the *shallit* persona. The dramatic-irony cuts sharp: Yosef the dream-interpreter (the Gen 40-41 *pitron*-master, governed by the central `pitron-dream-interpretation-yosef-cycle` entry, who explicitly attributes interpretive-knowledge to Elohim) is here framed as a Mesopotamian/Egyptian-style cup-diviner. The Gen 3 *nachash* serpent-homophony is a literary observation only (HALOT distinguishes the two lemmas; the etymological relation is debated and not here adjudicated). Governed by the new central `nachesh-divination-cup-yosef-cycle-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיַּשִּׂגֵ֑ם וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: And he overtook them, and he spake unto them these words.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו לָ֚מָּה יְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲדֹנִ֔י כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה חָלִ֙ילָה֙ לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ מֵעֲשׂ֖וֹת כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: And they said unto him, Wherefore speaketh my lord such words as these? Far be it from thy servants that they should do such a thing.

paragraphs.commentary: *Chalilah la-avadekha me'asot ka-davar ha-zeh* — 'far be it from thy servants that they should do such a thing' — deploys the corpus's standard ritual-disavowal formula. The construction is formally a feminine-noun-construct of *chol* / *chalal* ('profane / unholy'), used as an exclamation: 'be it profane / unholy [to me/us] to do this'. Cross-corpus reach saturates the corpus: Gen 18:25 (Avraham's intercession — the lexeme's first occurrence); 1 Sam 12:23 (Shemu'el); 14:45 (the people redeeming Yehonatan); 22:15; 24:7; 26:11; 2 Sam 20:20; 23:17; Job 27:5 (the climax of Iyov's integrity-declaration). The chapter-internal mirror at v 7 + v 17 — the brothers' *chalilah la-avadekha* echoed by Yosef's *chalilah li* — is the chapter's literary signature for the formula. The irony is sharp on both ends: the brothers' *chalilah* is undermined by their actual Gen 37 guilt; Yosef's *chalilah* is staged by his own test-setup. Governed by the new central `chalilah-far-be-it-disavowal-formula`.

paragraphs.text: הֵ֣ן כֶּ֗סֶף אֲשֶׁ֤ר מָצָ֙אנוּ֙ בְּפִ֣י אַמְתְּחֹתֵ֔ינוּ הֱשִׁיבֹ֥נוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן וְאֵ֗יךְ נִגְנֹב֙ מִבֵּ֣ית אֲדֹנֶ֔יךָ כֶּ֖סֶף א֥וֹ זָהָֽב׃

i18n.en: Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks' mouths, we brought again unto thee out of the land of Kena'an: how then should we steal out of thy lord's house silver or gold?

paragraphs.text: אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִמָּצֵ֥א אִתּ֛וֹ מֵעֲבָדֶ֖יךָ וָמֵ֑ת וְגַם־אֲנַ֕חְנוּ נִֽהְיֶ֥ה לַֽאדֹנִ֖י לַעֲבָדִֽים׃

i18n.en: With whomsoever of thy servants it be found, let him die, and we also will be my lord's bondmen.

paragraphs.commentary: The brothers' over-broad self-imprecatory oath — *asher yimmatze ito me-avadekha va-met ve-gam-anachnu nihyeh la-adoni la-avadim* — echoes Ya'aqov's analogous self-curse at Gen 31:32 (*im asher timtza et eloheikha lo yichyeh*) when Lavan accused Ya'aqov of stealing the *terafim*. The Gen 31:32 → Gen 44:9 echo is one of the corpus's most-noted boomeranging-oath structures: both involve a missing precious-object (Lavan's *terafim* / Yosef's silver-cup) hidden in the youngest-Rachel-line member's possessions (Rachel hides the *terafim*; Binyamin's sack contains the cup); both invoke a death-curse that the speaker does not realize will boomerang (Ya'aqov inadvertently curses Rachel; the brothers inadvertently curse Binyamin); both involve search-by-status. The literary parallel is widely documented (Alter, Sternberg, Sarna). Governed by the new overlay `self-curse-oath-formula-vamet-gen44`.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר גַּם־עַתָּ֥ה כְדִבְרֵיכֶ֖ם כֶּן־ה֑וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִמָּצֵ֤א אִתּוֹ֙ יִהְיֶה־לִּ֣י עָ֔בֶד וְאַתֶּ֖ם תִּהְי֥וּ נְקִיִּֽם׃

i18n.en: And he said, Now also let it be according unto your words: he with whom it is found shall be my bondman; and ye shall be blameless.

paragraphs.commentary: The steward softens the brothers' over-broad oath: instead of death-plus-collective-enslavement, he proposes individual-enslavement-for-the-finder and freedom-for-the-rest. The narrative-effect prepares the chapter's central dilemma: the test will isolate Binyamin from the brothers, replicating the Gen 37 isolation-of-Yosef that the brothers themselves engineered.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְמַהֲר֗וּ וַיּוֹרִ֛דוּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־אַמְתַּחְתּ֖וֹ אָ֑רְצָה וַֽיִּפְתְּח֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ אַמְתַּחְתּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Then they hasted, and took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.

paragraphs.text: וַיְחַפֵּ֕שׂ בַּגָּד֣וֹל הֵחֵ֔ל וּבַקָּטֹ֖ן כִּלָּ֑ה וַיִּמָּצֵא֙ הַגָּבִ֔יעַ בְּאַמְתַּ֖חַת בִּנְיָמִֽן׃

i18n.en: And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left off at the youngest: and the cup was found in Binyamin's sack.

paragraphs.commentary: *Ba-gadol hechel u-va-qaton killah* — 'began at the eldest, and left off at the youngest' — is the chapter's literary-structural search-order construction. The merism eldest→youngest is part of the cycle's persistent foregrounding of birth-order as a structural marker (cf. Gen 43:33's seating-order, governed by the sibling overlay `tamah-marvel-impossible-knowledge-seating-gen43`; Gen 48:13-20's crossed-hands blessing of Ephraim and Menasheh). The narratological function is suspense-prolongation: as each older brother's sack is searched and found innocent, the brothers' (false) relief grows and the impending revelation sharpens. Governed by the new overlay `search-by-birth-order-eldest-youngest-gen44`.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיִּקְרְע֖וּ שִׂמְלֹתָ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲמֹס֙ אִ֣ישׁ עַל־חֲמֹר֔וֹ וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ הָעִֽירָה׃

i18n.en: Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and returned to the city.

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-yiqre'u simlotam* — 'they rent their clothes' — deploys the standard HB grief-rending formula at the chapter's third Yosef-cycle occurrence. The triplet: Gen 37:29 (Re'uven at the empty pit, the cycle's first grief-rending); Gen 37:34 (Ya'aqov on receiving the bloodied tunic); Gen 44:13 (the ten brothers as collective-subject at the cup-discovery). The cross-corpus distribution is corpus-wide (Num 14:6; Josh 7:6; Judg 11:35; 2 Sam 1:11; 3:31; 13:31; 1 Kgs 21:27; 2 Kgs 2:12; 5:7; 6:30; 11:14; 18:37 = Isa 36:22; 19:1 = Isa 37:1; 22:11 + 19 = 2 Chr 34:19 + 27; Esth 4:1; Job 1:20; 2:12; Jer 36:24; Joel 2:13). The collective-subject of the Gen 44:13 occurrence distinguishes it from the two Gen 37 individual-subject occurrences: the same brothers who once engineered Re'uven's and Ya'aqov's grief now grieve themselves. Governed by the new overlay `qara-simlot-rent-garments-grief-formula-yosef-cycle`.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א יְהוּדָ֤ה וְאֶחָיו֙ בֵּ֣יתָה יוֹסֵ֔ף וְה֖וּא עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ שָׁ֑ם וַיִּפְּל֥וּ לְפָנָ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃

i18n.en: And Yehudah and his brethren came to Yosef's house; and he was yet there: and they fell before him on the ground.

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-yippelu lefanav artzah* — 'they fell before him on the ground' — is the third *hishtachavah*-fulfilment in the Yosef-cycle's dream-and-fulfilment arc (Gen 37:7 + 9 + 10 → 42:6 → 43:26 + 28 → 44:14 → 50:18). The verse uses *naphal artzah* — the *naphal* prostration-variant rather than the *hishtachavah* lexeme itself — but the dream-fulfilment-arc framing of the central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship` entry accommodates the variant: the entry's appliesTo is extended to include Gen 44:14 as a within-arc lexical variant. The chapter's literary point — that the third dream-fulfilment is staged with the variant prostration-formula rather than the dream-verb itself — is itself worth documenting: the brothers' prostration at the chapter's most-pressured moment is intensified by the *naphal*-variant (literally 'they fell to the ground'), naming the collapse-of-composure that the cup-discovery has produced. Yehudah's name appears first in the construction (*va-yavo Yehudah ve-echav*) — the chapter's marker that the speech-leadership of vv 18-34 is being introduced.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ יוֹסֵ֔ף מָֽה־הַמַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֑ם הֲל֣וֹא יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם כִּֽי־נַחֵ֧שׁ יְנַחֵ֛שׁ אִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּמֹֽנִי׃

i18n.en: And Yosef said unto them, What deed is this that ye have done? know ye not that such a man as I can indeed divine?

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's second *nachesh yenachesh* construction, now on Yosef's own lips. The chapter-internal pair (v 5 + v 15) intensifies the lexical-irony: the steward's accusation-on-Yosef's-behalf at v 5 is echoed by Yosef's direct pseudo-claim at v 15 (*nachesh yenachesh ish asher kamoni*, 'such a man as I can indeed divine'). The contradiction with Yosef's Gen 40-41 theology of dream-interpretation-as-divine-disclosure (Gen 40:8 *ha-lo le-Elohim pitronim*; Gen 41:16 *Elohim ya'aneh et shalom Par'oh*) is part of the maintained-disguise: as the *shallit*, Yosef adopts the Egyptian-court divinatory-persona to test the brothers. The reader who has tracked the Gen 40-41 theology knows the framing is part of the disguise, not Yosef's actual claim.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָ֗ה מַה־נֹּאמַר֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י מַה־נְּדַבֵּ֖ר וּמַה־נִּצְטַדָּ֑ק הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים מָצָא֙ אֶת־עֲוֺ֣ן עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ הִנֶּנּ֤וּ עֲבָדִים֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י גַּם־אֲנַ֕חְנוּ גַּ֛ם אֲשֶׁר־נִמְצָ֥א הַגָּבִ֖יעַ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Yehudah said, What shall we say unto my lord? what shall we speak? or how shall we clear ourselves? The Elohim hath found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold, we are my lord's bondmen, both we, and he also in whose hand the cup is found.

paragraphs.commentary: Yehudah's chapter-pivot verse loads three glossary-level lexemes in quick sequence. (i) *Mah-nitztaddaq* — 'how shall we clear ourselves' — deploys the rare Hithpael of *tzadaq* in the reflexive-declarative 'declare-oneself-righteous / clear-oneself' sense. The Yehudah-internal Gen 38:26 → Gen 44:16 *tzadaq*-arc traces the man who once declared Tamar *tzadqah mimmeni* ('she is more in the right than I') to the man who now declares his brothers' inability to *nitztaddaq*. The sibling-overlay pair `tzadqah-mimmeni-she-is-in-the-right` ↔ `nitztaddaq-hithpael-tzadaq-yehudah-arc-gen44` is the project's third overlay-overlay sibling-pair anchored at Gen 38 (after Gen 37↔38 *haker-na* and Gen 38↔43 *arav-eravon*), confirming Gen 38's load-bearing function as the cycle's Yehudah-character-development anchor-chapter. (ii) *Ha-Elohim matza et-avon avadekha* — 'Elohim hath found out the iniquity of thy servants' — is the Yosef-cycle's first explicit *avon*-naming and the brothers' second confession-of-guilt after the Gen 42:21 *ashemim* confession (which used the *asham* lexeme). The shift *asham* → *avon* across the Gen 42 → Gen 44 confession-arc escalates from naming-guilt-state to naming-comprehensive-iniquity. *Avon* is one of the HB's three principal sin-vocabulary terms (with *peshah* and *chatah*), with the three-fold semantic load (act / guilt / consequence); cross-corpus reach across Exod 20:5 + 34:7 (the divine-attribute formulae); Lev 16:21-22 (the scapegoat's iniquity-bearing); Isa 53:5-6 + 11 (the suffering-servant); Jer 31:34 (the New Covenant formula); Ezek 18 (the generational-iniquity debate); Ps 32:5 + 51:4 (the great confession-psalms). Governed by the new central `avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword` with bidirectional sibling-link to `avon-mins'so` (Gen 4:13). (iii) The chapter's single divine-name occurrence is *ha-Elohim* on Yehudah's lips — confirming the Yosef-cycle Elohim-default sustained; the chapter's narrator-voice carries zero divine-name. Yehudah's deliberate-openness — confessing comprehensively without confessing specifically — is the literary signature of his speech, preparing the way for Yosef's Gen 45 disclosure where the *avon* of Gen 37 is finally explicitly named.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר חָלִ֣ילָה לִּ֔י מֵעֲשׂ֖וֹת זֹ֑את הָאִ֡ישׁ אֲשֶׁר֩ נִמְצָ֨א הַגָּבִ֜יעַ בְּיָד֗וֹ ה֚וּא יִהְיֶה־לִּ֣י עָ֔בֶד וְאַתֶּ֕ם עֲל֥וּ לְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶל־אֲבִיכֶֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And he said, Far be it from me that I should do so: the man in whose hand the cup is found, he shall be my bondman; but as for you, get you up in peace unto your father.

paragraphs.commentary: Yosef's *chalilah li me'asot zot* — 'far be it from me that I should do so' — completes the chapter-internal mirror with the brothers' v 7 *chalilah la-avadekha*. Yosef refuses the brothers' collective-enslavement offer (the v 16 *hinennu avadim la-adoni*) and proposes the test-scenario that Yehudah's substitution-speech will respond to: Binyamin stays as slave, the brothers go up *le-shalom* ('in peace') to their father. The test is at its sharpest here: the chapter-staging now isolates Binyamin from the brothers, replicating exactly the Gen 37 isolation-of-Yosef that the brothers engineered (Yosef sold; the brothers free). Yosef's *le-shalom el avikhem* ('in peace unto your father') is the trigger of Yehudah's substitution-speech: returning to Ya'aqov without Binyamin is precisely what cannot be done, as vv 22-34 will document. The (פ) at the verse-end marks a Masoretic *parashah* break — the chapter's structural pivot between the test-statement and Yehudah's speech-response.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ אֵלָ֜יו יְהוּדָ֗ה וַיֹּאמֶר֮ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִי֒ יְדַבֶּר־נָ֨א עַבְדְּךָ֤ דָבָר֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י וְאַל־יִ֥חַר אַפְּךָ֖ בְּעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֥י כָמ֖וֹךָ כְּפַרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: Then Yehudah came near unto him, and said, Oh my lord, let thy servant, I pray thee, speak a word in my lord's ears, and let not thine anger burn against thy servant; for thou art even as Pharaoh.

paragraphs.commentary: Yehudah's surety-speech opens with the most extreme acknowledgment of Yosef's authority in the cycle: *ki khamokha ke-Par'oh* — 'for thou art even as Pharaoh'. The construction is essentially unique in the HB (no exact parallel of the *kha-X ke-Y* deferential-equation-to-the-monarch formula). The deference-formula is the structural-and-thematic counterpart of the Gen 37:8 brothers' refusal-of-Yosef's-dominion (*ha-malokh timlokh aleinu im-mashol timshol banu*, 'shalt thou indeed reign over us, or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us?'). The character-arc Gen 37:8 → Gen 44:18 traces Yehudah's complete reversal: from refusing-Yosef's-dominion to acknowledging-Yosef-as-monarch-equivalent. Rhetorically, the construction binds Yosef to monarchic-honor obligations (the duty to hear the petitioner) and prepares the speech's emotional-pressure architecture. Governed by the new overlay `ki-khamokha-ke-parah-deference-formula-gen44`.

paragraphs.text: אֲדֹנִ֣י שָׁאַ֔ל אֶת־עֲבָדָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר הֲיֵשׁ־לָכֶ֥ם אָ֖ב אוֹ־אָֽח׃

i18n.en: My lord asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father, or a brother?

paragraphs.text: וַנֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֔י יֶשׁ־לָ֙נוּ֙ אָ֣ב זָקֵ֔ן וְיֶ֥לֶד זְקֻנִ֖ים קָטָ֑ן וְאָחִ֨יו מֵ֜ת וַיִּוָּתֵ֨ר ה֧וּא לְבַדּ֛וֹ לְאִמּ֖וֹ וְאָבִ֥יו אֲהֵבֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And we said unto my lord, We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loveth him.

paragraphs.commentary: Yehudah's retelling deploys *ve-achiv met* ('and his brother is dead') — the brothers' first explicit *met*-statement of Yosef's death in the cycle. The lexical shift from *einennu* (the chapter-42 brothers' euphemism, charged with deliberate ambiguity) to *met* (the explicit death-claim) is marked: the brothers' Gen 42:13 + 32 *einennu* preserved the non-committal euphemism; here, in Yehudah's speech before the disguised Yosef, the death-claim is made explicit. The shift may signal Yehudah's rhetorical commitment to the conventional death-fiction (he speaks in the register Ya'aqov has adopted); or it may reflect the brothers' adoption of Ya'aqov's interpretive frame in the retelling. The *einennu*-refrain overlay's appliesTo is extended to include this verse alongside the chapter's other *einennu*-variant occurrences (vv 26, 30, 34) as the chapter's marked-break-and-resumption of the refrain. The *ben zequnim* construction (matching Gen 37:3's description of Yosef as Ya'aqov's *ben zequnim*) is now transferred to Binyamin — the patriarch's affection has migrated from the supposedly-dead Yosef to the surviving Rachel-line son.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ הוֹרִדֻ֖הוּ אֵלָ֑י וְאָשִׂ֥ימָה עֵינִ֖י עָלָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Bring him down unto me, that I may set mine eyes upon him.

paragraphs.text: וַנֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֲדֹנִ֔י לֹא־יוּכַ֥ל הַנַּ֖עַר לַעֲזֹ֣ב אֶת־אָבִ֑יו וְעָזַ֥ב אֶת־אָבִ֖יו וָמֵֽת׃

i18n.en: And we said unto my lord, The lad cannot leave his father: for if he should leave his father, his father would die.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ אִם־לֹ֥א יֵרֵ֛ד אֲחִיכֶ֥ם הַקָּטֹ֖ן אִתְּכֶ֑ם לֹ֥א תֹסִפ֖וּן לִרְא֥וֹת פָּנָֽי׃

i18n.en: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Except your youngest brother come down with you, ye shall see my face no more.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֙ כִּ֣י עָלִ֔ינוּ אֶֽל־עַבְדְּךָ֖ אָבִ֑י וַנַּ֨גֶּד־ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass when we came up unto thy servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָבִ֑ינוּ שֻׁ֖בוּ שִׁבְרוּ־לָ֥נוּ מְעַט־אֹֽכֶל׃

i18n.en: And our father said, Go again, buy us a little food.

paragraphs.text: וַנֹּ֕אמֶר לֹ֥א נוּכַ֖ל לָרֶ֑דֶת אִם־יֵשׁ֩ אָחִ֨ינוּ הַקָּטֹ֤ן אִתָּ֙נוּ֙ וְיָרַ֔דְנוּ כִּי־לֹ֣א נוּכַ֗ל לִרְאוֹת֙ פְּנֵ֣י הָאִ֔ישׁ וְאָחִ֥ינוּ הַקָּטֹ֖ן אֵינֶ֥נּוּ אִתָּֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: And we said, We cannot go down: if our youngest brother be with us, then will we go down; for we may not see the man's face, except our youngest brother be with us.

paragraphs.commentary: *Ve-achinu ha-qaton einennu ittanu* — 'except our youngest brother be with us' — deploys the chapter's first full *einennu*-construction (vv 20's *ve-achiv met* used the *met* variant; vv 26, 30, 34 use the *einennu* refrain proper). The Gen 37:30 → 42:13 + 32 + 36 → 44:26 + 30 + 34 cross-cycle arc is one of the corpus's tightest lexical-refrain structures. Yehudah's quadruple chapter-internal deployment of *einennu* climaxes the refrain: the brothers' false *einennu* once applied to Yosef (the absent-without-explanation euphemism of chapter 42) is now applied truthfully to the threat of Binyamin's loss. The overlay entry's appliesTo is extended to include all four chapter-44 *einennu*-construction occurrences.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר עַבְדְּךָ֥ אָבִ֖י אֵלֵ֑ינוּ אַתֶּ֣ם יְדַעְתֶּ֔ם כִּ֥י שְׁנַ֖יִם יָֽלְדָה־לִּ֥י אִשְׁתִּֽי׃

i18n.en: And thy servant my father said unto us, Ye know that my wife bare me two sons:

paragraphs.commentary: *Shenayim yaledah-li ishti* — 'my wife bare me two sons' — is one of the cycle's most concentrated literary markers of Ya'aqov's Rachel-centric grief. The construction's marked exclusivity is grammatically explicit: the singular *ishti* ('my wife') refers exclusively to Rachel (Le'ah, Bilhah, and Zilpah excluded from the wife-designation); *shenayim yaledah-li* names only Yosef and Binyamin as Ya'aqov's children (the ten elder brothers — sons of Le'ah, Bilhah, and Zilpah — excluded from the *yaledah-li shenayim* count). The phrasing is reported by Yehudah in the hearing of the ten brothers themselves — the patriarchal-erasure of the ten brothers is performed (by the patriarch) and reported (by one of the erased) in the same scene. The dramatic-irony: the ten brothers whose erasure-from-the-count their father performs are the same ones now offering themselves into slavery to save the other 'my wife's son'. The patriarchal-erasure is being inverted by the brothers' substitution-offer. Standard commentary (Sarna, Westermann, Alter, Hamilton) consensus reads the phrase as 'eloquent in its exclusiveness'. Governed by the new overlay `shenayim-yaledah-li-ishti-rachel-exclusive-wife-gen44`.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּצֵ֤א הָֽאֶחָד֙ מֵֽאִתִּ֔י וָאֹמַ֕ר אַ֖ךְ טָרֹ֣ף טֹרָ֑ף וְלֹ֥א רְאִיתִ֖יו עַד־הֵֽנָּה׃

i18n.en: And the one went out from me, and I said, Surely he is torn in pieces; and I have not seen him since:

paragraphs.commentary: *Akh tarof toraf* — 'surely he is torn in pieces' — is the verbatim repetition of Ya'aqov's Gen 37:33 conclusion on seeing the bloodied *ketonet passim*. The seven-chapter cross-chapter lexical-verbatim echo is one of the corpus's most concentrated literary structures, locking the patriarch's continued belief in the Gen 37 false-evidence: across twenty-two years of narrative-time, Ya'aqov has not revised his Gen 37 conclusion. Yehudah's deployment of his father's exact words — quoting Ya'aqov to the *shallit* in the patriarch's own paronomastic construction — surfaces the chapter's central dramatic-irony with concentrated force: Yosef hears his father's belief about his death reported by the brother who knows the truth, in the patriarch's own words. The companion overlay `chayah-raah-evil-or-wild-beast` governs the Gen 37 chapter-bracket *chayah ra'ah* construction (where the Gen 37:33 *tarof toraf* occurs paired with the wild-beast naming); this verse's overlay `tarof-toraf-paronomastic-torn-in-pieces-yaaqov-belief-gen37-44` governs the chapter-pair paronomastic-echo specifically. The two entries are bidirectional siblings per the ratified pattern.

paragraphs.text: וּלְקַחְתֶּ֧ם גַּם־אֶת־זֶ֛ה מֵעִ֥ם פָּנַ֖י וְקָרָ֣הוּ אָס֑וֹן וְהֽוֹרַדְתֶּ֧ם אֶת־שֵׂיבָתִ֛י בְּרָעָ֖ה שְׁאֹֽלָה׃

i18n.en: And if ye take this one also from me, and harm befall him, ye shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to She'ol.

paragraphs.commentary: Three Yosef-cycle Ya'aqov-internal lexemes converge at this verse, all extended in their appliesTo on the chapter-44 pass. (i) *Ason* (the marked fear-term for fatal mischance / lethal calamity) is now the third Yosef-cycle deployment (Gen 42:4 → 42:38 → 44:29) — ALL on Ya'aqov's lips, ALL about Binyamin, ALL about the journey-to-Mitsrayim; the entry's rationale already documents the three-occurrence Ya'aqov-internal fear-formula deployment. (ii) *Seivah* (the metonymic 'gray hairs' for aged old-age) is the second of three Yosef-cycle deployments (Gen 42:38 → 44:29 → 44:31) — also Ya'aqov-internal and bound to the descent-to-She'ol grief-formula. (iii) *She'olah* (the locative-directional 'down to She'ol') is the lexeme's second Yosef-cycle occurrence after Gen 42:38; the construction *seivah* + *She'olah* + descent-verb forms a fixed lament-formula, with the 1 Kgs 2:6 cross-corpus parallel (Shelomoh's *al toreid seivato be-shalom she'olah*) as its single external lexical-echo. The three lexemes' appliesTo extensions ratify the chapter-44 pass's documented continuation of the Ya'aqov-internal grief-arc.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה כְּבֹאִי֙ אֶל־עַבְדְּךָ֣ אָבִ֔י וְהַנַּ֖עַר אֵינֶ֣נּוּ אִתָּ֑נוּ וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹ קְשׁוּרָ֥ה בְנַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

i18n.en: Now therefore when I come to thy servant my father, and the lad is not with us; seeing that his life is bound up in the lad's life;

paragraphs.commentary: *Ve-ha-na'ar einennu ittanu* — 'and the lad is not with us' — deploys the chapter's second *einennu*-construction, now applied to Binyamin in Yehudah's hypothetical-return-to-Ya'aqov. The literary-irony is sharp: the same construction the brothers used falsely-euphemistically of Yosef in chapter 42 is now applied truthfully to the threatened Binyamin. The supplementary clause *ve-nafsho qeshurah ve-nafsho* ('his life is bound up in the lad's life') anatomizes the patriarchal love-bond — the Rachel-line son and the father bound in a single soul-tie. The chapter's emotional-architecture pivots on this naming: Yehudah makes audible to the *shallit* the patriarchal-bond that the test would destroy.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּרְאוֹת֛וֹ כִּי־אֵ֥ין הַנַּ֖עַר וָמֵ֑ת וְהוֹרִ֨ידוּ עֲבָדֶ֜יךָ אֶת־שֵׂיבַ֨ת עַבְדְּךָ֥ אָבִ֛ינוּ בְּיָג֖וֹן שְׁאֹֽלָה׃

i18n.en: it shall come to pass, when he seeth that the lad is not with us, that he will die: and thy servants shall bring down the gray hairs of thy servant our father with sorrow to She'ol.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's second occurrence of the descent-to-She'ol grief-formula. The construction *ki-ein ha-na'ar* deploys *ayin* (the negative-existential particle) WITHOUT the 3ms suffix — the variant form of the chapter's *einennu* refrain; the *einennu*-overlay entry's rationale notes the broader *ayin* + suffix construction is corpus-common, with the chapter-specific deployment as the entry's anchor. The Ya'aqov-internal grief-formula triplet (Gen 42:38 → 44:29 → 44:31) now closes its Yosef-cycle arc, with the central `sheol-underworld-realm-of-the-dead` and the overlay `seivah-gray-hairs-old-age-yaaqov-yosef-cycle` both extended in appliesTo. The literary force at this verse is the projected-consequence: Yehudah names the death-by-grief that the patriarch's loss-of-Binyamin would produce, completing the affective-pressure architecture of the substitution-speech.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י עַבְדְּךָ֙ עָרַ֣ב אֶת־הַנַּ֔עַר מֵעִ֥ם אָבִ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־לֹ֤א אֲבִיאֶ֙נּוּ֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְחָטָ֥אתִי לְאָבִ֖י כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃

i18n.en: For thy servant became surety for the lad unto my father, saying, If I bring him not unto thee, then shall I bear the blame to my father for ever.

paragraphs.commentary: *Avdekha arav et ha-na'ar* — 'thy servant became surety for the lad' — completes the Gen 43:9 → Gen 44:32 verbal-callback: the *arav*-pledge Yehudah made to Ya'aqov at Gen 43:9 (*anokhi e'ervennu mi-yadi tevaqshennu*) is now ratified-and-extended in Yehudah's speech before Yosef. The overlay entry's id (`arav-eravon-yehudah-surety-pledge-gen43-44`) explicitly implies the Gen 43-44 scope; the appliesTo is now extended to GEN-WOH-44:32. The bidirectional sibling-link to the Gen 38 *eravon*-pledge-triad overlay (`eravon-pledge-triad-signet-cord-staff`) is verified: the Gen 38 → Gen 43 → Gen 44 Yehudah-character-arc is the cycle's moral-literary fulcrum (the man who once GAVE a pledge — the *eravon* of signet, cord, and staff — now offers HIMSELF as the *arav*, the pledge-person). Standard scholarship: Alter, Sternberg, Fokkelman, Sarna all read the Gen 38 → Gen 43 → Gen 44 arc as the corpus's most concentrated Yehudah-character-development structure.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה יֵֽשֶׁב־נָ֤א עַבְדְּךָ֙ תַּ֣חַת הַנַּ֔עַר עֶ֖בֶד לַֽאדֹנִ֑י וְהַנַּ֖עַר יַ֥עַל עִם־אֶחָֽיו׃

i18n.en: Now therefore, let thy servant, I pray thee, abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter's moral-and-structural climax: Yehudah's substitution-offer *yeshev-na avdekha tachat ha-na'ar* — 'let thy servant abide instead of the lad'. The preposition *tachat* in its substitution-sense is one of the corpus's most-cited literary-theological patterns. The Gen 22:13 ↔ Gen 44:33 substitution-typology is the corpus's structural anchor: at Gen 22:13 (the Aqedah) Avraham offered the ram *tachat beno* ('in the stead of his son'), the external-substitute for Yitzchaq; at Gen 44:33 Yehudah offers HIMSELF — the self-substitute for Binyamin. The asymmetry traces a substitution-deepening from animal-substitute to self-substitute; the self-substitution's literary force is its voluntary and personal character. Cross-corpus reach across the *tachat* substitution-formula's principal occurrences: Exod 21:23-25 + Lev 24:18-20 (the lex talionis *nefesh tachat nefesh* / *ayin tachat ayin*); Num 3:12 + 41 + 45 (the Levites *tachat* the firstborn); Isa 53:5-10 (the suffering-servant's substitutionary suffering — conceptually paired even though the Isa 53 lexeme of choice is *mi-* and the *nasa avon* iniquity-bearing language). Named scholarship (Sternberg, Alter, Brueggemann, Fokkelman, Sarna) consensus reads the Gen 22:13 ↔ Gen 44:33 typological-pair as one of the corpus's most-cited literary observations. NO Christian-theological atonement-reading is here imposed: the typology is documented as named literary scholarship, not as a pre-commitment to substitutionary-atonement-theology. Governed by the new central `tachat-substitution-formula`.

paragraphs.text: כִּי־אֵיךְ֙ אֶֽעֱלֶ֣ה אֶל־אָבִ֔י וְהַנַּ֖עַר אֵינֶ֣נּוּ אִתִּ֑י פֶּ֚ן אֶרְאֶ֣ה בָרָ֔ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִמְצָ֖א אֶת־אָבִֽי׃

i18n.en: For how shall I go up to my father, if the lad be not with me? lest I see the evil that shall come on my father.

paragraphs.commentary: The chapter ends mid-speech with the fourth chapter-44 *einennu* occurrence: *ve-ha-na'ar einennu itti* — 'if the lad be not with me'. Yehudah's *ki-eikh e'eleh* peroration ('for how shall I go up to my father...') is broken off at the chapter-end — the speech does not conclude in chapter 44 but is left as the chapter's literary cliffhanger. The resolution comes at Gen 45:1's *ve-lo yakhol Yosef le-hit'appeq le-khol ha-nitzavim alav* ('and Yosef could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him') — the structural-pair collapse-point of the central `yitappaq-emotional-restraint-yosef-arc` entry. The Gen 43:31's *va-yit'appaq* (Yosef restraining himself after the *nikhmeru rachamav* compassion-burning) is here at Gen 45:1 reversed: Yosef's *yit'appaq* control finally fails under the pressure of Yehudah's surety-speech. The Yehudah-speech / Yosef-restraint-collapse pairing is the moral-and-structural climax of the cycle. The chapter's quadruple *einennu*-deployment (vv 20, 26, 30, 34) climaxes the Gen 37 → 42 → 44 refrain-arc, locking the lexeme at its most concentrated chapter-internal density before the Gen 45 disclosure that will retire the refrain.
